a needle-free injector can be designed to reproducibly eject a collagenase solution at a preprogrammed rate and pressure and that collagenase can be delivered to skin with the needle-free injector and produce a similar wound healing response to a conventional syringe.

the use of a Lorentz-force driven injector to deliver bacterial collagenase to skin results in the formation of necrotic tissue, hair loss and tissue remodeling that is comparable to the results obtained using conventional syringes.
the Lorentz-force injector is a viable alternative method for delivering collagenase to skin.

the use of an electrostatically actuated needle-free injection device as a means of delivering active collagenases into skin.

a needle-free injector can be used to deliver a drug to the skin with activity and efficacy comparable to that observed when the same drug is administered using conventional methods.

the Lorentz-force injector is a viable alternative to a conventional syringe and needle for delivery of collagenases to the epidermal/dermal layer of skin and that it may be useful for delivery of other therapeutics.
